newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota corn, soybeans aided by rain in week.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota corn, soybeans aided by rain in week.

text.p: Rains aided South Dakota corn and soybean maturity in the week ended September 8 but the state's soils still need more moisture for finishing row crops and winter seeding, the weekly state crop report said.
Temperatures were generally 2-4 degrees above normal in the week but good rains fell toward the weekend in most areas. Growing degree days were generally 20-40 days above normal.
Topsoils were rated 64 percent short to very short of moisture against 71 pct last week and subsoils 58 pct short or very short against 47 pct a week ago, the report said.
A few cooler days slowed corn growth and aided maturation. Corn doughing reached 84 percent against the five-year average of 86 pct. Corn was rated 68 pct good to excellent, 26 fair.
Corn dented 44 pct vs 32 week ago, 54 year ago, 56 avg.
Corn mature 6 pct vs 2 w/a, nil y/a, nil avg.

Soybeans dropping leaves increased to 35 pct against against 12 last week, 15 last year and 30 average. "The dry weather enhanced the earlier maturity but hindered full yield potential," the report said. Soybeans were rated 62 percent good to excellent and 32 percent fair.
Sorghum rated 59 percent good to excellent, 24 fair.
Sorghum mature 23 pct vs 8 w/a, 3 y/a, 12 avg.
Sunflowers rated 62 pct good to excellent, 28 fair.
Sunflowers mature 6 pct vs nil, w/a, 3 y/a, 9 avg.
Winter wheat seeded 8 pct vs 1 w/a, 13 y/a, 14 avg.
Winter rye seeded 5 pct vs 2 w/a, 14 y/a, 16 avg.
